changed_text.before: Malawi experiments show that communication requires work, incentives and contacts; measured gendered credibility differences did not establish a precise pooled adoption penalty.
changed_text.after: The Malawi experiments show that peer effort, communication and uptake can respond to rewards and contact structure; some unrewarded arms also produced communication and knowledge gains. Measured gendered credibility differences did not establish a precise pooled adoption penalty.

original_source.inspected: Copyedited 2018 advance version, printed pp.18–20, Tables5–6 and accompanying prose; original cached extraction independently reread by parent

evidence: Table5 observes communication activities without rewards; p19/Table6 shows knowledge gains in unrewarded AEDO/LF arms. Incentives change peer effort/adoption without proving universal necessity.
